title: GOEO Economic Assistance Grant
agency: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity
description: Discretionary post-performance grant program used by the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity to support business expansion, relocation, and job creation in Utah. Funds are typically tied to hitting agreed milestones such as new full-time jobs at or above county average wage, capital investment, or corporate expansion projects. Used across targeted industries including aerospace and defense, life sciences and healthcare innovation, software and IT, advanced manufacturing, energy, and financial services.
eligibilityText: Utah for-profit businesses creating new jobs or making capital investment in the state. Awards are discretionary, negotiated case-by-case with GOEO, and generally post-performance (paid after milestones are verified). Not intended for early-stage companies with no near-term hiring plans.

title: EDTIF — Economic Development Tax Increment Financing Tax Credit
agency: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity
description: Utah's flagship corporate incentive: a post-performance, refundable tax credit of up to 30% of new state tax revenues (income, payroll withholding, and sales taxes) generated by a company's expansion or relocation project, paid out over a period of up to 20 years. Aimed at competitive expansion projects in targeted industries such as aerospace, life sciences, IT and software, advanced manufacturing, distribution, and corporate headquarters.
eligibilityText: Project must be competitive with other states (Utah must be competing for the expansion), create new high-paying jobs — generally at least 110% of the county average wage — and obtain local government participation/incentive. Post-performance: credit is earned only after jobs and wages are documented on tax filings. Best fit for companies planning 50+ new jobs; smaller counts possible in rural counties.

title: REDTIF — Rural Economic Development Tax Increment Financing
agency: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity
description: Rural variant of the EDTIF tax credit with lower thresholds, designed to bring expansion projects and jobs to rural Utah counties. Post-performance refundable tax credit against new state tax revenue generated by the project. Fits manufacturing, agri-business, energy, outdoor products, remote operations centers, and other employers willing to locate or expand outside the Wasatch Front.
eligibilityText: Project must be located in a qualifying rural Utah county (generally counties of the 3rd through 6th class, i.e. outside Salt Lake, Utah, Davis, and Weber counties). Lower job-count and wage thresholds than standard EDTIF — new jobs generally must pay at least 100% of county average wage. Post-performance; requires local government participation.

title: Rural County Grant Program (Rural Opportunity Program)
agency: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity — Center for Rural Development
description: State-appropriated grants distributed to Utah's rural counties for business development, workforce, and infrastructure projects. Counties use the funds for local business grants, business incubation, workforce training, and economic development projects — businesses access the money by partnering with or applying through their county's economic development office. Common uses: equipment for expanding rural manufacturers, main-street business improvement, broadband-enabled remote work, and agri-tech.
eligibilityText: Funds flow to counties of the 3rd, 4th, 5th, or 6th class (rural counties — excludes Salt Lake, Utah, Davis, Weber). A business cannot apply to GOEO directly; it must go through its county economic development office, and each county sets its own sub-grant rules. Business must operate in the rural county receiving funds.

title: Utah SSBCI Loan Participation Program
agency: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity (US Treasury SSBCI)
description: Federally funded (State Small Business Credit Initiative) program in which the state purchases a participation in — or lends alongside — a private lender's loan to a Utah small business, reducing the lender's risk so deals that fall just short of bank criteria can close. Usable for working capital, equipment, real estate, and expansion. Relevant to manufacturers, service businesses, and startups with revenue that are near-bankable but under-collateralized.
eligibilityText: Utah small businesses (generally under 500 employees, and under roughly 750 employees per SSBCI rules) applying through a participating private lender — the state does not lend directly to the business. Loan proceeds cannot be used for passive real estate investment, lobbying, or repaying delinquent taxes. Business must operate in Utah.

title: Utah SSBCI Venture Capital Co-Investment Program
agency: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity (US Treasury SSBCI)
description: SSBCI-funded equity program that co-invests state-managed capital alongside qualified private venture investors into Utah startups, effectively extending a funded round. Targets high-growth technology companies — software, life sciences, deep tech, aerospace, fintech — that have a committed private lead investor and need additional capital to close the round.
eligibilityText: Utah-based, for-profit small businesses raising a priced equity or convertible round with a qualified private lead investor — the state only co-invests alongside private capital, never leads alone. SSBCI restrictions apply (roughly under 750 employees; no passive real estate or gambling businesses). Company must maintain Utah operations.

title: Utah Innovation Fund
agency: Utah Innovation Fund (state-created, university-affiliated seed fund)
description: State-created seed fund that makes equity investments (typically $50K to $500K) in early-stage companies commercializing technology connected to Utah's colleges and universities. Focus areas include life sciences and medical devices, deep tech, engineering, software, and energy — especially technologies licensed from or developed at Utah institutions of higher education, including by students, faculty, and recent alumni.
eligibilityText: Company must have a genuine affiliation with a Utah institution of higher education — e.g. technology licensed from a Utah university, or founders who are students, faculty, or recent graduates. Utah-based, for-profit, early-stage. This is an equity investment, not a grant: the fund takes ownership and expects venture-style returns.

title: WTC Utah STEP Export Grant
agency: World Trade Center Utah (SBA State Trade Expansion Program)
description: Reimbursement grants ($2,000–$15,000) that help Utah small businesses start or grow exporting: international trade show booths and travel, foreign market compliance and certifications (e.g. CE marking), website localization and translation, export training, and international marketing campaigns. Funded by the SBA's State Trade Expansion Program and administered by World Trade Center Utah. Fits manufacturers, consumer products, software, and ag companies pursuing international customers.
eligibilityText: Utah-based small businesses per SBA size standards, in business at least one year, with a product or service that is export-ready and majority US content. Reimbursement-based: the company spends first and is reimbursed for approved expenses. Cannot fund general operations.

title: Talent Ready Utah Workforce Training Partnerships
agency: Talent Ready Utah (Utah System of Higher Education / GOEO)
description: State workforce initiative that funds and brokers customized training partnerships between Utah employers and education providers: work-based learning, apprenticeships, industry-specific certificate programs, and talent pipeline development. Priority sectors include aerospace and defense, advanced manufacturing, healthcare, IT and software development, financial services, and construction trades. Value to a company is subsidized employee training and pipeline building rather than cash.
eligibilityText: Utah employers with concrete hiring or upskilling needs willing to partner with a Utah school, technical college, or university on curriculum. Benefits flow as funded training programs, not direct payments to the company. Best fit for companies hiring multiple workers into similar technical roles.

title: Utah APEX Accelerator (Government Contracting Assistance)
agency: Utah APEX Accelerator (formerly PTAC), hosted by GOEO
description: Free one-on-one counseling that helps Utah businesses win federal, state, and local government contracts: SAM.gov registration, UEI setup, small business certifications (8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB), finding and interpreting solicitations, capability statements, proposal review, and post-award compliance. Especially valuable for companies targeting defense (Hill Air Force Base), aerospace, IT services, construction, and manufacturing procurement.
eligibilityText: Free to any Utah business interested in government contracting. No size, industry, or stage restrictions, though counseling is oriented to companies with a sellable product or service. Provides services and advice, not funding.

title: Utah Small Business Development Center (SBDC) Network
agency: Utah SBDC (SBA-funded, hosted at Utah colleges)
description: Free, confidential business consulting through centers across Utah: business planning, financial modeling and projections, loan application packaging (SBA 7(a)/504 prep), market research, licensing, and growth strategy. A common on-ramp for companies preparing to apply for loans or state programs. Serves every industry, from main-street retail to tech startups.
eligibilityText: Free to any current or aspiring Utah small business owner. No funding is awarded — the value is expert consulting time and loan/grant application preparation help.

title: SCORE Utah — Free Business Mentoring
agency: SCORE (SBA resource partner)
description: Free, ongoing one-on-one mentoring from experienced executives and entrepreneurs, plus low-cost workshops, for small businesses at any stage. Utah chapters cover the Wasatch Front and beyond with remote mentoring statewide. Useful for first-time founders, business plan feedback, pricing, and preparing to approach lenders or investors.
eligibilityText: Free to anyone starting or running a small business in Utah. Mentoring and education only — no direct funding.

title: University of Utah PIVOT Center Ascender Grants
agency: University of Utah PIVOT Center
description: Commercialization gap funding for technologies and startups affiliated with the University of Utah: prototype development, key experiments, regulatory groundwork, and de-risking milestones that move university inventions toward licensing or startup formation. Strong fit for medical devices, therapeutics, diagnostics, materials, and engineering spinouts from the U.
eligibilityText: Restricted to University of Utah-affiliated technologies — typically inventions disclosed to the PIVOT Center or startups licensing U of U IP, with faculty/student/staff involvement. Not open to companies without a University of Utah connection.

title: Lassonde Entrepreneur Institute Startup Competitions
agency: Lassonde Entrepreneur Institute, University of Utah
description: Annual student startup competitions with non-dilutive cash prizes, including the Utah Entrepreneur Challenge (open to students at any Utah college or university), Opportunity Quest business-model competition, and Get Seeded micro-grants. Prize pools reach tens of thousands of dollars for winners, plus mentoring, workspace, and investor exposure. Any industry — software, consumer products, medtech, hardware.
eligibilityText: Team must include a currently enrolled college student — the Utah Entrepreneur Challenge accepts students from any Utah higher-ed institution; some tracks are University of Utah students only. Companies without a student founder are not eligible. Prizes are competitive and seasonal (typically fall–spring academic cycle).

title: Salt Lake City Economic Development Loan Fund (EDLF)
agency: Salt Lake City Department of Economic Development
description: Below-market gap financing ($10,000–$350,000) for businesses located in or relocating to Salt Lake City: working capital, equipment, tenant improvements, inventory, and job-creating expansion. Favorable terms for businesses in target areas, women- and minority-owned businesses, and projects that create jobs or activate commercial corridors. Fits retail, food, manufacturing, and service businesses as well as startups with revenue.
eligibilityText: Business must be located within Salt Lake City limits (not just Salt Lake County). Requires demonstrated ability to repay — typically revenue or strong projections plus owner equity injection; startups face higher scrutiny. Loan, not a grant: interest-bearing and secured where possible.

title: Salt Lake County Revolving Loan Fund
agency: Salt Lake County Office of Regional Development
description: County-administered revolving loan fund providing gap financing to small businesses in Salt Lake County that cannot obtain full conventional financing: equipment purchases, working capital, leasehold improvements, and expansion tied to job creation or retention. Typically paired with a bank loan or owner investment rather than serving as sole financing.
eligibilityText: Business must operate within Salt Lake County. Emphasis on job creation/retention, often for low-to-moderate-income workers per federal CDBG-linked rules. Loan requires repayment ability and collateral where available; not for startups with no revenue path.

title: Ogden City Business Improvement Grants (BIG)
agency: Ogden City Community & Economic Development
description: Matching grant program helping Ogden businesses improve commercial properties and storefronts — facade renovation, signage, interior build-out, and code-related improvements — to strengthen downtown and commercial corridors. Practical fit for retail, restaurants, and any business occupying commercial space in Ogden that is investing in its location.
eligibilityText: Business or property must be located within Ogden City, generally in eligible commercial areas. Matching grant: the business must fund a share of project costs, and work usually requires pre-approval before starting. Not for operating expenses, payroll, or businesses outside Ogden.

title: Utah Enterprise Zone Tax Credit
agency: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity / Utah State Tax Commission
description: State income tax credits for businesses that create jobs or invest in designated rural enterprise zones: per-job credits (larger for jobs paying above county average wage or with employer health insurance), plus credits for investment in plant and equipment and for rehabilitating vacant buildings. Fits manufacturers, processors, and employers expanding in rural Utah communities.
eligibilityText: Business must be located in a designated enterprise zone (rural municipalities and counties — Wasatch Front metro areas do not qualify). Retail businesses and certain other sectors are excluded by statute. Credits are non-refundable against Utah income tax, so the business needs Utah tax liability to benefit.

title: Utah Rural Jobs Program
agency: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity (via approved rural investment companies)
description: Growth capital program channeling state-incentivized private investment into rural Utah small businesses through approved rural investment companies, as loans or equity-like investments for expansion, equipment, and job creation. Targets agriculture and food processing, manufacturing, energy, tourism infrastructure, and other employers in small-population counties.
eligibilityText: Business must have fewer than roughly 150 employees and operate principally in a rural Utah county (generally counties under about 31,000 population or other qualifying areas). Capital comes from approved rural investment companies, not directly from the state — the company applies to those fund managers. Must remain in the rural area for the investment period.

title: Utah Microloan Fund
agency: Utah Microloan Fund (nonprofit CDFI)
description: Small loans (roughly $5,000–$50,000) for Utah entrepreneurs who cannot yet qualify for bank financing, including startups, home-based businesses, and underserved founders (women, minorities, refugees, low-income). Funds working capital, inventory, equipment, and startup costs, paired with free business coaching. Any industry.
eligibilityText: Utah small businesses and startups, including pre-revenue businesses with a credible plan. Personal guarantee typically required; credit history is considered but imperfect credit is not disqualifying. Loan amounts are small — not suitable for capital needs above roughly $50K.

title: Custom Fit Employee Training
agency: Utah System of Higher Education — Technical Colleges
description: State-subsidized custom training for Utah companies, delivered through Utah's technical colleges and select universities: the state pays a large share of the cost to train a company's employees in skills the company chooses — CNC machining, welding, software, safety certifications, leadership, and more. High value for manufacturers and technical employers upskilling their workforce.
eligibilityText: Utah employers training their own W-2 employees; training is delivered or arranged through the local technical college, which sets the subsidized rate. Benefit is discounted training, not cash. Availability and subsidy levels vary by college service region.

title: Women's Business Center of Utah
agency: Women's Business Center of Utah (SBA resource partner)
description: Free and low-cost business advising, training, and certification help for women entrepreneurs statewide, including rural Utah: business planning, marketing, financials, WOSB certification for government contracting, and lender preparation. Men are also served; programming centers women-owned businesses.
eligibilityText: Open to Utah entrepreneurs, with programming designed for women-owned businesses at any stage. Services and training only — no direct funding.

title: Utah Manufacturing Modernization Grant
agency: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity (with iMpact Utah)
description: Grant program helping small and mid-sized Utah manufacturers modernize: operational assessments, lean/process improvement, automation and Industry 4.0 adoption, and implementation projects that raise productivity and wages. Delivered with manufacturing consultants (e.g. iMpact Utah); grants offset assessment and implementation costs.
eligibilityText: Utah-based manufacturers, generally small-to-medium sized (roughly under 500 employees), with physical production operations in the state. Funds target modernization projects, not general working capital. Cost-share may be required; amounts are approximate and vary by round and appropriation.

title: Utah Defense Manufacturing Community Support (Hill AFB Supplier Ecosystem)
agency: Utah Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity / Utah Advanced Materials & Manufacturing Initiative
description: Ecosystem support for Utah companies entering the defense and aerospace supply chain around Hill Air Force Base: supplier readiness guidance, connections to primes and sustainment contracts, composites and advanced materials expertise, and cybersecurity compliance (CMMC) preparation resources. Aimed at machine shops, composites, electronics, MRO, and software companies pursuing defense work.
eligibilityText: Utah companies with capabilities relevant to aerospace and defense supply chains. This is a connection and readiness resource, not a funding award; contract revenue comes from winning actual defense procurements.
